title: Central Coast Office Fitout & Furniture: A Practical Planning Guide
excerpt: Connect your Central Coast premises, fitout budget, furniture order and delivery plan with an editable workplace brief.
author: Joe Kelley
metaTitle: Central Coast Office Fitout & Furniture Planning Guide | YOS
metaDescription: Plan a Central Coast office move or refresh. Compare fitout scope, desks, chairs, installed quotes and site access with a free editable workplace brief.
body:
## Start with the decision, not a product list

A Central Coast office move can involve three different decisions: whether the premises suit the business, what building work is needed, and which furniture makes the layout usable. Approving them separately can leave a gap between the floor plan, the budget and the day your team needs to move in.

Use this guide for a workplace in Gosford, West Gosford, Erina, Tuggerah, Wyong or the surrounding Central Coast. It is a briefing framework, not an assessment of a particular building or a promise of local prices or delivery times.

**Working download:** [Central Coast workplace brief (CSV)](/guides/central-coast-workplace-brief.csv). Open it in Excel or your spreadsheet app, replace the prompts with your own information and share the same brief with the appointed project team. No email is required.

## Choose the right service for the job

| Your situation | First decision | Useful route |
| --- | --- | --- |
| The current office needs new furniture | What can be retained and which settings need replacing? | [Central Coast office furniture](/office-furniture-central-coast) |
| A new tenancy needs partitions, finishes or services | What is included in the premises and who must investigate the gaps? | [Central Coast office and commercial fitout](/office-fitout-central-coast) |
| The move includes building works and furniture | Who owns the connected scope, approvals and delivery decisions? | [Client-side fitout project management](/office-fitout) |
| You know the exact product you want | Does the selected configuration suit the room and delivery address? | [Shop Your Office Furniture](https://www.yourofficefurniture.com.au/) |

YOS is Newcastle-based and supports Central Coast project briefs. We provide client-side fitout project management; appointed builders, appropriately licensed trades, designers and certification advisers perform their respective work. Site attendance, availability and scope are confirmed for the actual project. There is no YOS Central Coast walk-in showroom.

## 1. Measure how the office needs to work

Record the busiest normal day rather than assuming that every employee needs the same setting every day. Include focused work, meetings, visitors, storage, equipment and planned growth. Ask the people using the space what is missing before treating a larger tenancy or a larger furniture order as the answer.

- Record each room or zone against a measured floor plan.
- List retained furniture with its dimensions, condition and adjustment functions.
- Check desk, chair, drawer and storage-door movement together.
- Identify acoustic, accessibility, privacy and equipment questions for the relevant advisers.
- Record who will approve the layout and when that decision is needed.

For individual workstation needs, use [Comcare's computers and workstations guidance](https://www.comcare.gov.au/office-safety-tool/spaces/work-areas/computers-workstations) and obtain suitable workplace-specific advice where required. A furniture label alone is not a workplace assessment.

## 2. Check the tenancy before promising an opening date

A furnished office, a warm shell and a cold shell can require very different work. Those descriptions are not an agreed schedule of inclusions. Request a written record of the existing ceilings, floors, lighting, mechanical services, power, data and amenities, then identify what needs investigation or modification.

Ask the landlord or building manager about access, building rules and the division between landlord works and tenant works. Ask the relevant appointed advisers about the intended use, approval pathway and design requirements. Do not assume a previous office use establishes that every proposed alteration can proceed without approval.

[Central Coast Council's permits and approvals guidance](https://www.centralcoast.nsw.gov.au/business/permits-and-approvals) recommends contacting its team about required approvals before signing a lease or renovating. Confirm the requirements for the actual premises with Council and your appointed advisers; this guide does not determine an approval outcome.

## 3. Build a budget that includes the missing items

Use a budget register rather than relying on one construction rate per square metre. A small office with substantial services changes can have a different cost profile from a larger office retaining an existing layout. Furniture, professional fees and moving costs may sit outside the quoted construction figure.

| Budget line | What to make visible |
| --- | --- |
| Design and investigations | Measured survey, design scope, services investigations and any specialist advice |
| Approvals and certification | Required application, inspection and certification responsibilities and costs |
| Construction and services | Documented building works, exclusions, assumptions and services changes |
| Furniture and equipment | New and retained products, quantities, accessories, IT and AV interfaces |
| Delivery and occupation | Freight, assembly, placement, moving, temporary accommodation and disruption |
| Allowances | Unquoted items, contingency, GST treatment and the owner of each estimate |

Our [fitout estimator](/resources/fitout-estimator) is an indicative planning tool. Check its location and scope assumptions. Its output is not a Central Coast tender or a confirmed price for your premises. Replace assumptions with site investigations and current itemised quotes as the design develops.

## 4. Compare the same scope across proposals

Ask each provider to price the same revision of the brief. An alternative can be valuable, but it should be separate from the base proposal so you can see what changes.

For fitout proposals, compare scope, quantities, exclusions, approval responsibilities, programme dependencies and the process for variations. For furniture, compare the actual range, product codes, dimensions, finishes, accessories and written warranty terms. Keep freight, assembly, installation, placement and packaging removal visible as separate inclusions.

**Illustrative example, not a client result:** two proposals include the same number of desks, but only one includes assembly and placement upstairs. Their unit prices do not tell you which complete order is cheaper or suitable for the building. Resolve the access and installation scope before approving either proposal.

## 5. Treat Central Coast delivery as a site-specific task

The suburb or postcode is the starting point, not the full delivery brief. A ground-floor workplace and an upstairs suite in the same area can have different access requirements.

1. Give the supplier the address, loading point and arrival contact.
2. Check stairs, lifts, doorway dimensions and the largest packaged item.
3. Confirm booking windows, building induction and protection requirements.
4. Agree who receives goods and resolves placement questions.
5. Confirm when the site will be ready for furniture and who checks that readiness.
6. Record delivered quantities, damage, outstanding work and the follow-up owner.

Do not treat a dispatch estimate as a confirmed installation date. Product availability, quantity, selected finishes, address eligibility and access arrangements need to be checked for the actual order.

## 6. Assign the connected decisions

Keep one short register with a decision, responsible person, required evidence and due date. That makes interfaces visible without assuming one provider takes every responsibility.

- The business approves its brief, budget and commercial commitments.
- The appointed designer and specialist advisers resolve their design scope.
- The builder and relevant trades carry out their contracted construction work.
- The relevant authority and certification advisers address the applicable approval requirements.
- The furniture supplier confirms product specifications and agreed supply services.
- A client-side project manager coordinates the agreed process and reports decisions back to the client.

YOS's [office fitout project management video](/videos/office-fitout-project-management) explains why a clear decision owner matters when a change affects more than one part of the project.

## A briefing checklist before you request quotes

- Confirm the premises address, project stage and target occupation date.
- Attach a measured plan or list the measurements still needed.
- Record current and future workplace requirements.
- Audit retained furniture and equipment.
- Identify building services and landlord works requiring confirmation.
- Ask the appropriate advisers about the use and approvals.
- Create a budget register with inclusions, exclusions and unpriced items.
- Label rooms and furniture items consistently across the plan and schedule.
- Confirm delivery access and site-readiness dependencies.
- Nominate who approves scope, purchases and changes.
- Keep handover documents and the outstanding-items list together.

## Get help with your Central Coast workplace

For construction-related changes, start with [Central Coast office and commercial fitout planning](/office-fitout-central-coast). For desks, chairs, meeting settings or a wider furniture order, use [Central Coast office furniture planning and supply](/office-furniture-central-coast).

Send your suburb, project stage, team requirements and target timing. We can discuss the next decisions and confirm whether the YOS scope suits the brief. Product choices, project attendance and delivery commitments are confirmed through the actual engagement and quote process.

[Download the workplace brief](/guides/central-coast-workplace-brief.csv) to organise the conversation.
